title: Your News Rule

launchpad.outcome: Decide your response to scheduled events before the session, and never invent one live.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What does my rule say when an event is scheduled?

slides.title: Scheduled. Known ahead of time.
slides.example: No new entries within 5 minutes before selected high-impact events.

rows.text: A valid Dayli ICC setup forms.

asks.prompt: Under that rule, the 9:57 setup is…

options.label: TAKE: it’s valid
options.feedback: Valid setup, 3 minutes before the event. The rule says no new entries within 5.

options.label: PASS
options.why: Valid setup. The news rule blocks participation.

asks.prompt: 10:04: it went on to win. Was passing wrong?

options.label: Yes, it won
options.feedback: Rule following doesn’t need the market to punish the trade you skipped.

options.label: No
options.why: RULE FOLLOWING DOES NOT REQUIRE THE MARKET TO PUNISH THE TRADE YOU SKIPPED.

lines: “Never trade news.” (unless that’s your tested rule)

slides.title: Build YOUR news rule
slides.punch: No template is universally correct. Use the one you’ll actually follow, then test it.

slides.title: An event in 3 minutes. No news rule defined.

options.label: Invent a 5-minute blackout for you
options.feedback: The Academy never invents your rules.

options.label: Flag it: NEWS RESPONSE NOT DEFINED
options.why: Something to resolve in Review Mode, before the next session.

slides.quote: The calendar is public. Your response to it should be too, at least to you.

slides.prompt: What is your news rule, and why that one?
slides.modelAnswer: My rule is decided before the session, for the events I selected. I don’t invent it live, and I follow it even when the skipped setup wins.

takeaways: Scheduled events are known in advance.
Define your response, don’t improvise it.
Undefined → flag it, never invent it.
remember: “I FORGOT NEWS WAS COMING OUT” IS A PREPARATION PROBLEM.
